source.name: sp_GetInventorySnapshot
source.sourceDefinition:
CREATE PROCEDURE dbo.sp_GetInventorySnapshot
AS
BEGIN
    SET NOCOUNT ON;

    -- Uses NOLOCK hint (dirty reads for performance)
    SELECT
        p.ProductID,
        p.ProductName,
        p.StockQuantity,
        p.Price
    FROM dbo.Products p WITH (NOLOCK)
    WHERE p.StockQuantity > 0
    ORDER BY p.StockQuantity ASC;
END;

result.generatedDdl:
CREATE OR REPLACE FUNCTION dbo.sp_GetInventorySnapshot()
RETURNS TABLE (
    ProductID INTEGER,
    ProductName TEXT,
    StockQuantity INTEGER,
    Price NUMERIC
)
LANGUAGE plpgsql
AS $$
BEGIN
    -- PostgreSQL uses MVCC; no equivalent to NOLOCK needed
    -- Returns result set directly
    RETURN QUERY
    SELECT
        p.ProductID,
        p.ProductName,
        p.StockQuantity,
        p.Price
    FROM dbo.Products p
    WHERE p.StockQuantity > 0
    ORDER BY p.StockQuantity ASC;
END;
$$;
assumptions: ProductID is mapped to INTEGER (assuming INT in SQL Server)
ProductName is mapped to TEXT (assuming VARCHAR/NVARCHAR in SQL Server)
StockQuantity is mapped to INTEGER (assuming INT in SQL Server)
Price is mapped to NUMERIC (assuming DECIMAL/MONEY in SQL Server)
The dbo schema exists in PostgreSQL or will be created
The Products table has been migrated with the same column names and compatible types
SET NOCOUNT ON is not needed in PostgreSQL functions (no row count messages by default)
The procedure returns a result set, so it's converted to a FUNCTION returning TABLE

reviewFlags.reason: Column data types are assumed based on common mappings. Verify actual column types in the Products table match the function signature (ProductID, ProductName, StockQuantity, Price types)
Verify that the dbo schema exists in PostgreSQL and the Products table has been migrated. PostgreSQL is case-sensitive with quoted identifiers

compatibilityNotes.description: SQL Server's WITH (NOLOCK) hint allows dirty reads (READ UNCOMMITTED isolation). PostgreSQL uses MVCC (Multi-Version Concurrency Control) and does not support dirty reads. The default READ COMMITTED isolation level in PostgreSQL provides consistent snapshots without blocking, which is generally safer than NOLOCK while still providing good performance

SQL Server stored procedure returns result set implicitly. PostgreSQL requires explicit FUNCTION with RETURNS TABLE or SETOF. Calling syntax changes from EXEC sp_GetInventorySnapshot to SELECT * FROM sp_GetInventorySnapshot()
PostgreSQL functions do not send row count messages by default, so SET NOCOUNT ON is unnecessary and has been omitted
